---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

---
name: hgraph
description: The dependency graph — Horizon's vendored hgraph core keeps one file per statement/Lean declaration under <project>/hgraph/; `horizon graph frontier` ranks work and agents attach node-scoped comments and reviews. This is the only DAG engine.
---

Each project may carry an **hgraph**: a plain-files semantic graph under
`<project>/hgraph/` — one Markdown node per blueprint statement and per Lean
declaration, typed edges (`uses` = the hard dependency DAG, `formalizes` =
informal↔formal identity). `horizon graph sync` (run automatically at run boundaries)
reconciles the blueprint + Lean sources into it; your **authored** additions
(comments, reviews, metadata) are never touched by sync. The files are
committed to the workspace ledger like everything else.

Use `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …`; when a workspace has one project,
`-p` is optional. Address nodes by `label:<latex-label>` or
`decl:<lean-fqname>` — raw ids are opaque hashes. Most commands accept `--json`.

## Sync it yourself — and act on the warnings

Don't wait for the run boundary: after you change blueprint statements,
`\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations, or Lean declarations, run
`"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> sync` and **read its output**. Sync prints warnings for exactly the defects
you can fix on the spot: `\uses{X} has no blueprint node` (missing/mistyped
label), `\lean{Name} not found in Lean sources` (renamed or unwritten
declaration), stale nodes whose source vanished. Fix what your change caused
before moving on; a warning you deliberately leave (e.g. a forward reference
you'll write next) gets a node comment or a memory item so the next session
knows it's intentional. Sync is idempotent and never touches your authored
comments/reviews/metadata.

## Read

- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> list --state ready` — nodes whose dependencies are all closed:
  provable *now*. Other states: `closed`, `blocked`, `formalized_open`.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` — the ready nodes ranked by how many downstream nodes a
  proof would unlock. **Use this when picking the next node to prove.**
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:thm:foo` — one node: statement, `lean_status`
  (`lean_ok | mathlib_ok | sorry | empty`, derived from scanning the Lean, not
  from `\leanok`), deps, attached comments/reviews.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> ancestors label:thm:foo` — the dependency cone.
- `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> stats` — per-state counts for the project.

## Write — per-node progress lives WITH the node

- **Comment = failure memory / progress note on that node.** When an approach
  fails or you learn something node-specific, record it where the next session
  will look first:
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add comment label:thm:foo --content "tried simp+ring, fails because …"`
  Agent authorship plus run/session/task provenance are filled from the run
  environment; do not copy the note into the blueprint.
- **Review = a Maths / Lean verdict** (independent axes, `good|bad`):
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> add review label:thm:foo --maths good --lean bad --lean-comment "statement ok; proof has a sorry at the succ case"`
- **Metadata**: `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> modify node label:thm:foo --set status=verified`

Prefer node comments over inbox items for anything scoped to ONE node; use the
inbox (skill: `horizon-inbox`) for cross-node or cross-session coordination.

An edge `source --uses--> target` means *source depends on target*. A node is
"ready" when all of its dependencies are closed; prefer `frontier`, which ranks
ready nodes by what they unlock. The dashboard provides the workspace project
switcher and the chapter-collapsed Graphviz view.

## Relation to the blueprint

The DAG **is** the hgraph — there is no second engine and no parser fallback.
It is generated by resolving the blueprint's `\uses{}`/`\lean{}` annotations
against the real Lean sources, so keeping those annotations correct (skill:
`blueprint-conventions`) is exactly what keeps this graph correct. Unresolved
references surface as `horizon graph sync` warnings and as `dangling` entries — read
the warnings rather than trusting `dangling` alone.

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

    43	question is a proof, not a redesign.

    10	
    11	`Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean` builds the general-test pullback `pullGlobal` of an
    12	affine divisor package `DivRepAffinePullback` together with its naturality in the
    13	test object.  This file supplies the other half — the general-test classifier — and
    14	assembles the `DivRepGlobalData` of `Picard/DivRepKit.lean`, hence the divisor
    15	representability of `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
    16	
    17	The classifier is obtained by gluing the landed affine classifiers `divRepClassifyZar`
    18	over the affine opens of the test.  Two observations make the gluing cheap:
    19	
    20	* The affine opens of a scheme form a **locally directed** open cover
    21	  (`Scheme.directedAffineCover`), so a morphism glues from compatibility with the
    22	  transition maps alone (`Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected`); no
    23	  condition on the — in general non-affine — overlaps is needed.
    24	* The required compatibility is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar` in the test algebra.
    25	  That naturality is not proved from the characterizing clause: it is *forced* by the
    26	  affine package, since `D.pull` is injective (`DivRepAffinePullback.equiv`) and natural
    27	  (`D.pull_naturality`), so the classifier — its inverse — is natural as well.
    28	
    29	The results:
    30	
    31	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.classifyGlobal` — the general-test classifier,
    32	  restricting at every affine open `W ⊆ T.left` to the affine classifier of the value
    33	  `F.1 W` (`fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal`).
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.toGlobalData` — the `DivRepGlobalData` of the
    35	  affine package: `pullGlobal` and `classifyGlobal` are mutually inverse on every test.
    36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.representableBy` — **the divisor
    37	  representability theorem in its conditional form**: an affine divisor package
    38	  represents `divFunctor C π g` by `DivScheme`.
    39	-/

    62	/-- The comparison isomorphism of an affine open with the spectrum of its section ring
    63	carries `IsAffineOpen.fromSpec` to the open immersion of the open. -/
    64	private theorem isoSpec_hom_fromSpec {X : Scheme.{u}} {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    65	    hU.isoSpec.hom ≫ hU.fromSpec = U.ι := by
    66	  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]
    67	
    68	/-- **Separation of test objects over their affine-open test objects**: two morphisms
    69	out of a test object `T` agreeing on every affine-open test object `Over.fromSpecAffine T U`
    70	are equal.  The affine opens cover `T.left`, and `fromSpecAffine T U` differs from the
    71	open immersion of `U` by the comparison isomorphism of `U`. -/
    72	private theorem hom_ext_fromSpecAffine {T Y : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (a b : T ⟶ Y)
    73	    (h : ∀ U : T.left.affineOpens,
    74	      Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ a = Over.fromSpecAffine T U ≫ b) :
    75	    a = b := by
    76	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
    77	  refine Scheme.Cover.hom_ext T.left.directedAffineCover _ _ fun U => ?_
    78	  have hU : U.2.fromSpec ≫ a.left = U.2.fromSpec ≫ b.left :=
    79	    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (h U)
    80	  change U.1.ι ≫ a.left = U.1.ι ≫ b.left
    81	  rw [← isoSpec_hom_fromSpec U.2, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hU]
    82	
    83	end Separation

   120	/-! ## Naturality of the affine classifier -/
   121	
   122	/-- **The affine backward classifier is natural in the test algebra.**  This is not
   123	proved from the characterizing clause: it is forced by the affine package, whose forward
   124	map `D.pull` is injective and natural, so its inverse is natural too — concretely, the
   125	base change of a classifier classifies the base-changed class, by
   126	`D.isDivRepClassify_pull` at the base-changed morphism. -/
   127	private theorem overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar
   128	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   129	    {A B : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
   130	    (phi : A →ₐ[k] B) (F : DivFamZar C A pi g) :
   131	    Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F
   132	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 B (DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F) := by
   133	  have hpull : D.pull B
   134	      (Over.overSpecMap phi ≫ divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F)
   135	      = DivFamZar.mapAlgHom phi F := by
   136	    rw [D.pull_naturality phi (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 A F),
   137	      D.pull_classify A F]
   138	  refine divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _ ?_
   139	  rw [← hpull]
   140	  exact D.isDivRepClassify_pull B _
   141	
   142	/-! ## The general-test classifier -/
   143	
   144	/-- The affine classifiers of the values of `F`, transported to the open subschemes of
   145	the affine opens of `T.left` — the family glued by `classifyGlobal`. -/
   146	private noncomputable def classifyPiece
   147	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   148	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) : U.1.toScheme ⟶ (DivOver).left :=
   149	  U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫
   150	    (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left
   151	
   152	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   153	-- The rewrite chain unifies through the section-ring algebra towers over both affine
   154	-- opens at once, so it exceeds the default elaboration budget (as in
   155	-- `divFamZar.exists_isGlueValue`).
   156	/-- The gluing datum: the family `classifyPiece` is compatible with the transition maps
   157	of the directed cover of `T.left` by its affine opens.  This is naturality of the affine
   158	classifier along the section restriction, applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
   159	private theorem homOfLE_classifyPiece
   160	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   161	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   162	    {U V : T.left.affineOpens} (hle : U.1 ≤ V.1) :
   163	    T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
   164	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
   165	  have hres : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left ≫ V.2.fromSpec
   166	      = U.2.fromSpec :=
   167	    congrArg CategoryTheory.Over.Hom.left (Over.fromSpecAffine_resAlgHom (T := T) hle)
   168	  have hkey : U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫ (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
   169	      = T.left.homOfLE hle ≫ V.2.isoSpec.hom := by
   170	    rw [← cancel_mono V.2.fromSpec, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hres,
   171	      isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, isoSpec_hom_fromSpec, Scheme.homOfLE_ι]
   172	  have hcl : (Over.overSpecMap (Over.resAlgHom T hle)).left
   173	        ≫ (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, V.1) (F.1 V)).left
   174	      = (divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, U.1) (F.1 U)).left := by
   175	    rw [← CategoryTheory.Over.comp_left,
   176	      overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D, F.compat U V hle]
   177	  rw [classifyPiece, classifyPiece, ← Category.assoc, ← hkey, Category.assoc, hcl]
   178	
   179	/-- The gluing datum: each piece lies over `Spec k` compatibly with the test `T`. -/
   180	private theorem classifyPiece_over
   181	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   182	    (U : T.left.affineOpens) :
   183	    classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U ≫ (DivOver).hom = U.1.ι ≫ T.hom := by
   184	  rw [classifyPiece, Category.assoc, CategoryTheory.Over.w,
   185	    ← CategoryTheory.Over.w (Over.fromSpecAffine T U), ← Category.assoc]
   186	  exact congrArg (· ≫ T.hom) (isoSpec_hom_fromSpec U.2)
   187	
   188	private theorem classifyPiece_trans
   189	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   190	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   191	    {U V : T.left.directedAffineCover.I₀} (hij : U ⟶ V) :
   192	    Scheme.Cover.trans T.left.directedAffineCover hij
   193	        ≫ classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F V
   194	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F U := by
   195	  rw [Subsingleton.elim hij (homOfLE (leOfHom hij)),
   196	    Scheme.directedAffineCover_trans (leOfHom hij)]
   197	  exact homOfLE_classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F (leOfHom hij)
   198	
   199	/-- **The general-test classifier of the affine package**: the affine classifiers of the
   200	values of `F` at the affine opens of `T.left`, glued over the locally directed cover of
   201	`T.left` by its affine opens.  The gluing datum is the compatibility with the transition
   202	maps `T.left.homOfLE`, which is naturality of `divRepClassifyZar`
   203	(`overSpecMap_comp_divRepClassifyZar`) applied to the coherence of `F`. -/
   204	noncomputable def classifyGlobal
   205	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   206	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) : T ⟶ DivOver :=
   207	  Scheme.OpenCover.glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected (X := T) (Y := DivOver)
   208	    T.left.directedAffineCover (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
   209	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
   210	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
   211	
   212	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   213	/-- The general-test classifier restricts on the open subscheme of an affine open to the
   214	transported affine classifier there. -/
   215	private theorem ι_classifyGlobal
   216	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   217	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   218	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
   219	    W.1.ι ≫ (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
   220	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F).left
   221	      = classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F W :=
   222	  Scheme.OpenCover.map_glueMorphismsOverOfLocallyDirected_left
   223	    (X := T) (Y := DivOver) T.left.directedAffineCover
   224	    (classifyPiece hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F)
   225	    (fun {_U _V} hij => classifyPiece_trans hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F hij)
   226	    (classifyPiece_over hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 F) W
   227	
   228	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   229	/-- **The characterizing property of the general-test classifier**: its restriction to
   230	the affine-open test object presented by `W` is the affine classifier of the value of `F`
   231	at `W`. -/
   232	theorem fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal
   233	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   234	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T)
   235	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
   236	    Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
   237	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
   238	      = divRepClassifyZar hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 Γ(T.left, W.1) (F.1 W) := by
   239	  refine Over.OverMorphism.ext ?_
   240	  change W.2.fromSpec ≫ _ = _
   241	  rw [← IsAffineOpen.isoSpec_inv_ι, Category.assoc,
   242	    ι_classifyGlobal hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 D F W, classifyPiece,
   243	    Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc]
   244	
   245	/-! ## The two inverse laws -/
   246	
   247	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   248	/-- **The `pull_classify` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test pullback of the
   249	general-test classifier of `F` is `F`.  Both sides are sections of the Zariski vehicle,
   250	so it suffices to compare at an affine open, where the characterizing property of the
   251	classifier reduces the statement to the affine law `D.pull_classify`. -/
   252	theorem pullGlobal_classifyGlobal
   253	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   254	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (F : divFamZar C pi g T) :
   255	    pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   256	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
   257	        (classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
   258	          (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F)
   259	      = F := by
   260	  refine divFamZar.ext fun W => ?_
   261	  rw [pullGlobal_val, fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, D.pull_classify]
   262	
   263	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   264	/-- **The `classify_pull` law at an arbitrary test**: the general-test classifier of the
   265	general-test pullback of `v` is `v`.  Morphisms out of a test are separated by the
   266	affine-open test objects, and at each of those the uniqueness theorem
   267	`divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify`, applied to `D.isDivRepClassify_pull`,
   268	identifies the affine classifier with the restriction of `v`. -/
   269	theorem classifyGlobal_pullGlobal
   270	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   271	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
   272	    classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   273	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D
   274	        (pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   275	          (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)
   276	      = v := by
   277	  refine hom_ext_fromSpecAffine _ _ fun W => ?_
   278	  rw [fromSpecAffine_classifyGlobal, pullGlobal_val]
   279	  exact (divRepClassifyZar_eq_of_isDivRepClassify hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2 _ _
   280	    (D.isDivRepClassify_pull _ (Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ v))).symm
   281	
   282	/-! ## The affine-to-general lift -/
   283	
   284	/-- **The affine-to-general lift of DDR-9.F7**: an affine divisor package determines the
   285	general-test data of `DivRepGlobalData` — the pullback is `pullGlobal`, the classifier is
   286	`classifyGlobal`, the two inverse laws are `classifyGlobal_pullGlobal` and
   287	`pullGlobal_classifyGlobal`, and naturality in the test object is `pullGlobal_comp`. -/
   288	noncomputable def toGlobalData
   289	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
   290	    DivRepGlobalData hpi g r1 r2 b1 b2 where
   291	  pull {_T} v := pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
   292	    (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
   293	  classify {_T} F := classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
   294	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
   295	  classify_pull {_T} v := classifyGlobal_pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
   296	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v
   297	  pull_classify {_T} F := pullGlobal_classifyGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO)
   298	    (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D F
   299	  pull_comp {_T _T'} f v := pullGlobal_comp (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
   300	    (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v
   301	
   302	/-- **Divisor representability from an affine package** (DDR-9.F7): an affine divisor
   303	package represents the locally certified divisor functor `divFunctor C π g` by
   304	`DivScheme`.  This is the composite of the affine-to-general lift with the categorical
   305	packaging `DivRepGlobalData.representableBy`. -/
   306	noncomputable def representableBy
   307	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2) :
   308	    (divFunctor C pi g).RepresentableBy DivOver :=
   309	  DivRepGlobalData.representableBy (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1)
   310	    (b2 := b2)
   311	    (toGlobalData (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   312	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D)
   313	
   314	end DivRepAffinePullback

    13	/-!
    14	# The ε frame cover, keyed on the WINDOW QUOTIENT rather than on a carrier
    15	
    16	Roadmap leaf `AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.framecover-aff`.
    17	
    18	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFraming.lean` established that the ε-pair and its pair-chart framing
    19	clause are expressible over the widened carrier, and recorded what it did not do:
    20	
    21	> It does not prove `exists_certChartCover` over the widened carrier — that theorem's proof
    22	> runs the certificate cover and the per-piece frame covers, which is real work and belongs to
    23	> whoever restates it.
    24	
    25	**This file measures that work, and the measurement is the content.**  Inside
    26	`exists_frame_chart_at_prime` the frame-cover keystone `divFamEps_exists_frameCover`
    27	(`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:456`) reads its carrier `DivFam C S π g` at **eight** sites, of
    28	**two** kinds:
    29	
    30	* **six** are facts about the window *quotient* — `DivFam.finite_/projective_window_quotient`
    31	  at each of the two ledger windows (:347–357), and `F.window` in the `exists_away_free_pair`
    32	  call (:361, :365).  Constant fibre rank enters separately, through `divFamWindowGr`'s own
    33	  definition.  These are what the layer below restates as hypotheses.
    34	* **two** are *functoriality* of the carrier: `DivFam.window_mapAlg` in the closing `rfl` blocks
    35	  (:426, :443), i.e. "window of `mapAlg` = `windowBaseChange`".  These are **not** window-quotient
    36	  facts, and they are exactly what `windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange` below had to replace.
    37	
    38	Everything downstream of the helper — `exists_component_matrix`,
    39	`exists_det_submatrix_notMem_of_mul_eq_one`, `exists_away_isUnit_of_notMem`,
    40	`map_component_chart` — consumes a Grassmannian *point* and a base ring, and never asks what
    41	produced the submodule.
    42	
    43	*A predecessor version of this paragraph said "exactly three points" and listed
    44	finite/projective/rankAtStalk.  That both under-counted the reads and mis-classified the two
    45	that motivated this file's one new theorem; corrected here (audit `I-1336`).*
    46	
    47	`divisorWindow d hH1` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:103`) is independent of the
    48	**adaptation** — of which cover refines `d` — which is what lets the declarations below typecheck
    49	carrier-free.  It is **not** independent of the pinned charts: it is a `Submodule.comap` of
    50	`d.vanishingSubmodule R (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ … .V₁ …`, so the fixed two-chart pair
    51	occurs in its definition.  *A predecessor version said "no adaptation, no cover and no chart
    52	typing"; only the first clause is true (`I-1336`).*
    53	
    54	## The one step that is genuinely new
    55	
    56	Restating the layer with the three facts as hypotheses is free, but the tower transport is
    57	not.  The chart-typed `map_divFamWindowGr` (`Picard/DivSchemeFrameCover.lean:188`) proves
    58	`Grassmannian.map β (point over R_h) = point over R_u` by routing through the divisor
    59	*object* — `DivFam.window_mapAlg` on both legs plus `DivFam.mapAlg_comp` — which needs a
    60	carrier with a functorial `mapAlg`.  Carrier-free there is no object to route through, so the
    61	composite must be proved where it actually lives, on the submodule:
    62	
    63	* `windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange` — transitivity of the window pushforward over a tower
    64	  `R → R' → R''`, for an arbitrary `k`-module ambient `H`.  Not in the tree before; both
    65	  inclusions are `windowBaseChange_le_iff` against the compared generators, and the content
    66	  is one `cancelBaseChange` compatibility (`rfl` fails on it, checked).

    68	## What this does and does NOT establish
    69	
    70	It does **not** produce a widened divisor-representability, and no antecedent of
    71	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` moves.  The window-quotient facts are **hypotheses** in the window
    72	layer.  The `Reachability` section below gives the chart-typed route to them; the correct ledger
    73	for the *widened* route is:
    74	
    75	  the frame cover's chart dependence   REMOVED (this file, sorry-free)
    76	  its window-quotient inputs           reachable chart-typed (below), and reachable WIDENED by
    77	                                       the same three-line proofs through

    79	                                       (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean:914`) — whose source
    80	                                       is the SAME quotient — gated on surjectivity of the

    83	**Two corrections to predecessor versions of this docstring, both from an audit
    84	(`I-1335`/`I-1337`) that I reproduced before accepting.**  I first wrote that the inputs "reduce
    85	to widened evaluation surjectivity"; I then over-corrected to "the ONE route that exists" plus

    87	retract loudly:

    89	* the widened route **exists** and is gated on a *missing proof*, not on a refutation;

   210	theorem windowBaseChange_windowBaseChange {H : Type u} [AddCommGroup H] [Module k H]
   211	    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   212	    (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
   213	    (R'' : Type u) [CommRing R''] [Algebra k R''] [Algebra R R''] [Algebra R' R'']
   214	    [IsScalarTower k R R''] [IsScalarTower k R' R''] [IsScalarTower R R' R'']
   215	    (N : Submodule R (R ⊗[k] H)) :
   216	    windowBaseChange R'' (windowBaseChange R' N) = windowBaseChange R'' N := by
   217	  -- the `R'`-linear comparison arrow `R' ⊗[k] H → R'' ⊗[k] H` of the upper leg
   218	  set ψ : (R' ⊗[k] H) →ₗ[R'] (R'' ⊗[k] H) :=
   219	    (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R' R'' R'' H).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
   220	      (TensorProduct.mk R' R'' (R' ⊗[k] H) 1) with hψdef
   221	  have hψ : ∀ y : R' ⊗[k] H, ψ y
   222	      = TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R' R'' R'' H (1 ⊗ₜ y) :=
   223	    fun _ => rfl
   224	  -- the tower compatibility of the comparison: the two legs agree on the lower generators
   225	  have key : ∀ x : R ⊗[k] H,
   226	      ψ (TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R R' R' H (1 ⊗ₜ x))
   227	        = TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange k R R'' R'' H (1 ⊗ₜ x) := by
   228	    intro x
   229	    induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
   230	    | zero => simp
   231	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [TensorProduct.tmul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   232	    | tmul r h => simp [hψ]
   233	  refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
   234	  · -- `⊆`: test the upper generators, then the lower ones through `ψ`
   235	    rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   236	    have hstep : windowBaseChange R' N
   237	        ≤ Submodule.comap ψ ((windowBaseChange R'' N).restrictScalars R') := by
   238	      rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   239	      intro x hx
   240	      refine Submodule.mem_comap.mpr ?_
   241	      rw [key x]
   242	      exact cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange hx
   243	    intro y hy
   244	    rw [← hψ y]
   245	    exact hstep hy
   246	  · -- `⊇`: a lower generator is `ψ` of an upper generator
   247	    rw [windowBaseChange_le_iff]
   248	    intro x hx
   249	    rw [← key x, hψ]
   250	    exact cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange
   251	      (cancelBaseChange_one_tmul_mem_windowBaseChange hx)

   408	      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤)) ⧸ divisorWindow d ha1) :=

     9	/-!
    10	# A DD-R CONSUMER ON THE WIDENED FUNCTOR (R2): `pullGlobal` read at `divFunctorAff`
    11	
    12	The widened carrier of protection I-0492 acquired a base-change face (ADDENDUM 8), a Zariski
    13	gluing keystone (§8.6), and finally a functor `divFunctorAff` with a natural transformation
    14	`divFunctorToAff` out of the chart-typed one (ADDENDUM 9).  What it did **not** have, at every
    15	one of those milestones, is a **consumer**: measured at HEAD, the widened names appeared in zero
    16	files outside the `Picard/DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` family.
    17	
    18	That is the gap this file closes.  It restates the DD-R general-test pullback
    19	(`DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobal`, `Picard/DivRepGlobalLift.lean`) on the widened functor and
    20	proves the `pull_comp` law there — the one field of `DivRepGlobalData` that is *about* the
    21	functor rather than about a single test.
    22	
    23	## What the restatement costs, and why that is the point
    24	
    25	Nothing but a push-forward.  `pullGlobalAff` is `divFamZarToAffVehicle ∘ pullGlobal`, and its
    26	naturality is the chart-typed `pullGlobal_comp` transported along `divFamZarToAffVehicle_map`.
    27	No gluing is redone and no certificate is re-derived over a widened cover.
    28	
    29	That cheapness is the substantive claim: it says the widened layer is *usable* by the existing
    30	DD-R stack, not merely well-formed.  A functor nothing consumes and a functor everything can
    31	consume look identical to a sorry census and to a job count.
    32	
    33	## Direction, once more
    34	
    35	Old → new.  A consumer that already produces a chart-typed section gets its widened counterpart
    36	for free.  The converse does not exist and cannot: by `informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 /
    37	ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 a straddling divisor at genus `≥ 2` is confined by no fixed pair of `P¹` charts.
    38	So this file does **not** claim the widened functor is representable by `DivOver`; it claims the
    39	chart-typed representability datum pushes forward to a compatible family of widened values.
    40	
    41	## Main declarations
    42	
    43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobalAff` — the widened general-test pullback.
    44	* `…pullGlobalAff_val` — its value at an affine open, `toAff` of the chart-typed one.
    45	* `…pullGlobalAff_comp` — the `pull_comp` law at `divFamZarAff.map`.
    46	* `…divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_pullGlobalAff` — affine consistency, through the widened collapse.
    47	-/

    99	namespace DivRepAffinePullback

   101	/-! ## The widened general-test pullback -/
   102	
   103	-- No `[IsAffineHom pi]` binder here: the file-level `[IsFinite pi]` already implies it, and
   104	-- carrying both made every declaration below report an overlapping-instance warning.
   105	
   106	/-- **The widened general-test pullback**: the chart-typed `pullGlobal` pushed forward along the
   107	vehicle comparison of R2.  Its value at an affine open is the widened value of the chart-typed
   108	one, so a consumer that already has the affine package gets the widened section with no extra
   109	input. -/
   110	noncomputable def pullGlobalAff
   111	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   112	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver) : divFamZarAff C g T :=
   113	  divFamZarToAffVehicle C g pi
   114	    (pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   115	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)
   116	
   117	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   118	/-- The value of the widened general-test pullback at an affine open. -/
   119	@[simp]
   120	theorem pullGlobalAff_val
   121	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   122	    {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (v : T ⟶ DivOver)
   123	    (W : T.left.affineOpens) :
   124	    (pullGlobalAff (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   125	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v).1 W
   126	      = (D.pull Γ(T.left, W.1) (Over.fromSpecAffine T W ≫ v)).toAff :=
   127	  rfl
   128	
   129	/-! ## Naturality in the test object, at the WIDENED functor -/
   130	
   131	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   132	/-- **The `pull_comp` law on the widened functor**: the widened general-test pullback is natural
   133	in the test object, with the *widened* glued restriction `divFamZarAff.map`.
   134	
   135	This is the field of `DivRepGlobalData` that is about the functor rather than about one test, and
   136	it is the statement that makes the widened layer consumable.  The proof is the chart-typed
   137	`pullGlobal_comp` transported along the naturality of the vehicle comparison
   138	(`divFamZarToAffVehicle_map`) — no gluing is redone. -/
   139	theorem pullGlobalAff_comp
   140	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   141	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))} (f : T' ⟶ T) (v : T ⟶ DivOver) :
   142	    pullGlobalAff (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   143	        (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D (f ≫ v)
   144	      = divFamZarAff.map C g f
   145	          (pullGlobalAff (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1)
   146	            (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v) := by
   147	  show divFamZarToAffVehicle C g pi _ = _
   148	  rw [pullGlobal_comp (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   149	      (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D f v,
   150	    divFamZarToAffVehicle_map f]
   151	  -- Both sides are now `divFamZarAff.map C g f` applied to the same term, but the right-hand one
   152	  -- still wears the folded name `pullGlobalAff`.  That unfolding is definitional and `rw`'s
   153	  -- terminal `rfl` runs at reducible transparency only, so it must be discharged explicitly.
   154	  rfl
   155	
   156	set_option linter.unusedSectionVars false in
   157	/-- **Affine consistency of the widened pullback**: on an affine test it collapses through the
   158	widened comparison `divFamZarAffAffineEquiv` to the widened value of the affine pullback. -/
   159	theorem divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_pullGlobalAff
   160	    (D : DivRepAffinePullback hpi g hO hchi r1 r2 b1 b2)
   161	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (v : overSpec k A ⟶ DivOver) :
   162	    divFamZarAffAffineEquiv C g A
   163	        (pullGlobalAff (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi) (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2)
   164	          (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D v)
   165	      = (D.pull A v).toAff := by
   166	  rw [pullGlobalAff, divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_toAffVehicle,
   167	    divFamZarAffineEquiv_pullGlobal (hpi := hpi) (g := g) (hO := hO) (hchi := hchi)
   168	      (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) D A v]
   169	
   170	end DivRepAffinePullback

   424	
   425	A predecessor of this file carried a theorem `not_reachable_of_straddling` here, asserting "the
   426	route above is unavailable exactly on the divisors R2 exists for".  **It is withdrawn**, and the
   427	reasoning is kept in its place because that is the reusable part (audit `I-1334`/`I-1335`/
   428	`I-1337`, reproduced before accepting).

   430	Three things were wrong with it:
   431

   433	   (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean:127`) — same binders, same conclusion, body a direct
   434	   delegation — and that lemma is in this file's own import closure, so the restatement served
   435	   nobody;
   436	2. it carried `[IsNoetherianRing R]`, which its proof does not use;
   437	3. and the claim it was there to support is **false**.  The reachability theorems above are

   439	   hypotheses runs through `AffAdaptation.windowQuotEquiv`, over `AffAdaptation`, which the

   443	   widened carrier is the one that works.
   444	
   445	What is true, and all that is true: the three theorems above are the **chart-typed** supply of

    78	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
    79	system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
    80	the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
    81	`FinCoverData`. -/
    82	structure CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff (n : ℕ) : Type u where
    83	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/

    85	  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/

    96	/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
    97	(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over

   102	CURVE, and changes nothing about the Zariski cover of the base. -/

   108	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (g i)) n,
   109	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   110	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   111	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   112	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))

   125	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))

   128	/-! ## The comparison with the chart-typed predicate
   129	
   130	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER
   131	sorry-free, and the adaptation's equations and `eqn_rel` transport with it because the pieces
   132	are literally the same opens, only reindexed along `finSumFinEquiv`.
   133	
   134	The migration of the CERTIFICATE is landed too, in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`
   135	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff`, all seven clauses).  Clauses (c1) are `rfl` at the
   136	relabelled index; the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`
   137	in its `symm` direction, which evaluates cast-free, so the intertwining with
   138	`deltaLeft`/`deltaRight` is componentwise and `Module.rankAtStalk` invariance is
   139	`rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv`.  No clause changes, only the index does.
   140	
   141	A predecessor docstring here estimated that transport at about a hundred lines of equalizer
   142	bookkeeping.  That was wrong by an order of magnitude and the reason generalises: arrange the
   143	reindexed cover so its pieces are DEFINITIONALLY the original pieces at the relabelled index,
   144	and the overlap data at `(i, j)` becomes `rfl`-equal to the original at `(e i, e j)`, because
   145	reindexing acts diagonally on the pair index.  Then no intertwining lemma exists to prove. -/

    11	/-!
    12	# The global theta cokernel and the widened intrinsic range
    13	
    14	A widened certificate supplies fibrewise vanishing for `O(a Theta - d)`.  After choosing
    15	an auxiliary chart presentation of the same local equations, the existing rigid engine
    16	turns those witnesses into vanishing of the first cohomology of its theta-ideal sheaf.
    17	The canonical sheaf inclusion from `DivisorThetaSheafSequence` therefore has a surjective
    18	cokernel projection on global sections.
    19	
    20	The range of that inclusion on global sections is exactly the cover-independent vanishing
    21	submodule.  Hence the cokernel is canonically the same quotient already identified with
    22	the range of intrinsic widened theta evaluation.  No chart typing of the widened cover and
    23	no additional hypothesis occur.
    24	-/

    46	    (hc : A.IsCertified g) (a : Nat) (h : D.SwallowedBy d)
    47	    (p : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    48	    Module.rankAtStalk (A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a) p = g := by
    49	  obtain ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩ := h
    50	  let e : A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := pi) a ≃ₗ[R]
    51	      A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0 :=
    52	    (A.intrinsicThetaGluedEquivPieceProdOfSwallowedBy
    53	      (pi := pi) a ⟨j0, hsub, hmiss⟩).trans
    54	        (A.thetaPieceProdEquivSwallowingPiece (pi := pi) a hmiss)
    55	  have hpiece : Module.rankAtStalk
    56	      (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) p =
    57	      Module.rankAtStalk (A.colength j0) p := by
    58	    letI : Module.Finite R (A.colength j0) := hc.finite_colength j0
    59	    letI : Module.Projective R (A.colength j0) := hc.projective_colength j0

    61	        (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) :=
    62	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
    63	    letI : Module.Invertible (A.colength j0)
    64	        (A.ThetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0) :=
    65	      A.invertible_thetaPieceQuotient (π := pi) a j0

    68	    let ecol : A.Glued ≃ₗ[R] A.colength j0 :=

   146	/- The `AlgHom`-induced algebra structures on `Localization.Away (g i)` and `K` make the
   147	`divEq_mapAlg_pullback` unifier work through two towers; within the DivSchemeAbel precedent. -/
   148	/-- **Over a field, every widened locally certified system is divisor-equal to a globally
   149	certified widened family** — the widened `DivFam.exists_toZar_eq`
   150	(`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:77`), stated at the level of systems rather than of classes.
   151	
   152	A span-`⊤` family over a field has a nonzero member, which is a unit, so
   153	`Localization.Away (g i)` is `K` itself (`IsLocalization.atUnits`); the local certified family
   154	base-changes back along that isomorphism, and the composite pullback collapses by
   155	`relCurveMap_id`.  Every step is about the base, so the widening is invisible here.
   156	
   157	**The `DivEq` conclusion is deliberate and is what makes this cheap.**  The class-level form
   158	`∃ G, G.toZarAff = F₀` would need `toZarAff (F.mapAlg R' n hinf) = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n
   159	F.toZarAff`, which does not exist in the tree; the consumer
   160	(`AffAdaptation.deg_presentationDivisor_of_divEq`) wants a `DivEq` anyway, so the quotient
   161	level is never re-entered. -/
   162	theorem exists_certifiedAff_divEq (d : (relCurve C K).LocalEquations)
   163	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) :
   164	    ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C K n, Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns d := by
   165	  obtain ⟨m, g, hspan, hG⟩ := id hd
   166	  -- some member of the span-⊤ family is nonzero
   167	  have hex : ∃ i, g i ≠ 0 := by
   168	    by_contra hall
   169	    have hall' : ∀ i, g i = 0 := fun i => by
   170	      by_contra hi
   171	      exact hall ⟨i, hi⟩
   172	    have hle : Ideal.span (Set.range g) ≤ ⊥ := Ideal.span_le.mpr (by
   173	      rintro x ⟨i, rfl⟩
   174	      rw [SetLike.mem_coe, Ideal.mem_bot]
   175	      exact hall' i)
   176	    rw [hspan, top_le_iff] at hle
   177	    exact one_ne_zero (Ideal.mem_bot.mp (hle ▸ Submodule.mem_top (x := (1 : K))))
   178	  obtain ⟨i, hgi⟩ := hex
   179	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C K (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   180	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C K (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   181	  obtain ⟨Gᵢ, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
   182	  -- the away localization at a unit is `K` itself
   183	  have hunits : Submonoid.powers (g i) ≤ IsUnit.submonoid K := by
   184	    rintro x ⟨e, rfl⟩
   185	    exact (isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hgi).pow e
   186	  haveI : IsLocalization (Submonoid.powers (g i)) K :=
   187	    IsLocalization.of_le_isUnit hunits
   188	  let e₀ : K ≃ₐ[K] Localization.Away (g i) :=
   189	    IsLocalization.atUnits K (Submonoid.powers (g i)) hunits
   190	  let e : Localization.Away (g i) ≃ₐ[k] K := e₀.symm.restrictScalars k
   191	  letI : Algebra (Localization.Away (g i)) K := e.toAlgHom.toRingHom.toAlgebra
   192	  haveI : IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away (g i)) K :=
   193	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (e.commutes a).symm
   194	  have hKA : ∀ a : K, e (algebraMap K (Localization.Away (g i)) a) = a := by
   195	    intro a
   196	    change e₀.symm (algebraMap K (Localization.Away (g i)) a) = a
   197	    rw [← e₀.commutes a]
   198	    exact e₀.symm_apply_apply _
   199	  haveI : IsScalarTower K (Localization.Away (g i)) K :=
   200	    .of_algebraMap_eq fun a => (hKA a).symm
   201	  -- base change the local family back to `K` and collapse the composite pullback
   202	  refine ⟨Gᵢ.mapAlg K n Gᵢ.cover.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper, ?_⟩
   203	  refine (CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.divEq_mapAlg_pullback n K Gᵢ
   204	    Gᵢ.cover.hasAffineOverlaps_of_isProper
   205	    (hd.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors K n) hGdiv).trans ?_
   206	  exact Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback_id relCurveMap_id d _

   247	/-- **`toZarAff` commutes with base change**: the class of a base-changed widened certified

   251	absence `I-1187` and conversation `I-1190` both priced as this row's remaining cost.  It is one
   252	line: both sides are `mk` of the pulled system — `CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.mapAlg`'s `eqns`
   253	field *is* `pulledEquations`, which *is* the pullback along the comparison, with the regularity
   254	proof irrelevant — so `mk_eq_mk_iff` reduces the goal to `divEq_refl`. -/
   255	theorem CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff.toZarAff_mapAlg {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   256	    (R' : Type u) [CommRing R'] [Algebra k R'] [Algebra R R'] [IsScalarTower k R R']
   257	    (F : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C R n) (hinf : F.cover.HasAffineOverlaps) :
   258	    (F.mapAlg R' n hinf).toZarAff = DivFamZarAff.mapAlg R' n F.toZarAff :=
   259	  DivFamZarAff.mk_eq_mk_iff.mpr (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl _)
   260	
   261	/-- **The widened field collapse at the quotient level** — the exact analogue of
   262	`DivFam.exists_toZar_eq` (`Picard/DivSchemeAbel.lean:77`): over a field every widened class is
   263	the class of a *globally* certified widened family.

     9	# Widened-adaptation extraction (R2, human decision I-0492)
    10	
    11	**Every** local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a widened adaptation, with no
    12	chart input whatsoever: `AffAdaptation.exists` below is the R2 counterpart of
    13	`exists_divisorAdaptation` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyExtraction.lean`).
    14	
    15	## Why this is the shape the widening was for
    16	
    17	The chart-typed extraction runs the affine-refinement engine **on each of the two pinned
    18	charts** and glues the results with a partition of unity per chart — the partitions are what
    19	`exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` produces, and they are exactly what protection I-0492
    20	ordered deleted.  Here there is nothing to glue: affine opens form a basis of any scheme
    21	(`Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens`), the relative curve is quasi-compact when `C` is (being a base
    22	change of `C.left`), so one pass gives a finite affine-open cover subordinated to `d.cover`.
    23	No `π`, no charts, no partitions, no `Sum` index.
    24	
    25	The comparison unit is `1` at every piece, as in the chart-typed extraction: the equation is
    26	literally the restriction of `d`'s equation at the anchor.
    27	
    28	## Main declarations
    29	
    30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instQuasiCompactRelCurveHom`, `instCompactSpaceRelCurve` — the relative
    31	  curve over a proper `C` is quasi-compact over its test base, hence compact.
    32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affCoverData_subordinate` — a finite affine-open cover with, per
    33	  piece, an anchor point of `d.cover` whose member contains the piece.
    34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation` — hence a widened adaptation of `d`.
    35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper` — the same with the compactness
    36	  hypothesis discharged, so with NO hypothesis on the system.
    37	
    38	## What this does and does not close
    39	
    40	It closes the *adaptation* half of the widened lane's producer gap: before this file, the only
    41	way to obtain an `AffAdaptation` was `FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` plus
    42	`DivisorAdaptation.toAff` — i.e. through the chart-typed predicate, which is exactly the route
    43	R2 exists to avoid.  Now a widened adaptation exists for every system, directly.
    44	
    45	It does NOT produce a *certificate*.  The two obligations protection I-0492 clause 4 relocated
    46	— fibrewise-finite support and `SwallowedBy` — remain obligations, and a cover produced by this
    47	extraction has no reason to have a straddling piece.  Producing one that does is where the
    48	Stacks `0B8B` input enters, and that is still owed.

   104	  -- extract a finite subcover

   113	            pieces := fun j => W (e j).1
   114	            isAffineOpen := fun j => hWaff (e j).1

   116	    fun j => (e j).1, fun j => hWle (e j).1⟩
   117	  refine top_le_iff.mp fun z _ => ?_
   118	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hzs⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp (ht (Set.mem_univ z))

   130	    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
   131	    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩⟩

   141	    (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
   142	    ∃ D : AffCoverData C R, Nonempty (AffAdaptation D d) :=
   143	  exists_affAdaptation C R d

     9	# Finite transport for the widened intrinsic theta range
    10	
    11	The global cokernel argument supplies surjectivity of the intrinsic high-window carve on an
    12	arbitrary affine-open cover.  Since the high window is finite over the test ring, its image is
    13	finite as well.  This file records that output in the exact quotient shape consumed by the
    14	frame layer, and transports the certified glued-algebra module facts to the equalizer algebra
    15	carrier used by the intrinsic Cech module.
    16	
    17	No chart typing and no certificate clause are added here.  Projectivity and rank of the
    18	intrinsic theta module still require the effective-descent invertibility seam; this file makes
    19	the finite part and the equalizer-algebra transport available independently of that seam.

    65	theorem IsCertified.finite_intrinsicThetaGluedOver
    66	    (hc : A.IsCertified g)

    68	    (hO : Sheaf.h0 (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1)
    69	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    70	    (ha1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π
    71	      (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    72	    (hMa : windowM_choice π hπ g ≤ a) :
    73	    Module.Finite (↥(gluedSubalgebra A))
    74	      (A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a) := by
    75	  let M := A.IntrinsicThetaGluedOver (π := π) a
    76	  let AD := ↥(gluedSubalgebra A)
    77	  letI : Module R M := Module.compHom M (algebraMap R AD)
    78	  letI : IsScalarTower R AD M :=
    79	    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul fun _ _ => rfl
    80	  haveI : Module.Finite k
    81	      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤) :=

    90	    Module.Finite.of_surjective
    91	      (A.intrinsicThetaEvalRel (π := π) a)
    92	      (AlgebraicGeometry.AffAdaptation.IsCertified.intrinsicThetaEvalRel_surjective
    93	        C R π hc hπ hO hχ ha1 hMa)
    94	  let e : M ≃ₗ[R] A.IntrinsicThetaGlued (π := π) a :=
    95	    { toFun := fun x => ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
    96	      invFun := fun x => ⟨x.1, x.2⟩
    97	      map_add' := fun _ _ => rfl
